newsitem.title: USA: Northwest to buy KLM holding with cash.
newsitem.headline: Northwest to buy KLM holding with cash.

text.p: Northwest Airlines Corp said Wednesday it will use its cash reserves to buy about $1.0 billion of its stock from KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV as part of an agreement to end a dispute between the carriers.
"It will be paid from our cash reserves. We've got $1.0 billion in cash on hand," Douglas Killian, director of international communications at Northwest, said.

Earlier, Northwest and KLM said they agreed in principle to extend their existing operating alliance and for KLM to sell its 19 percent voting stock position in Northwest to the St. Paul, Minn.-based airline.
KLM also agreed to end its pending legal actions against Northwest, which stemmed from a dispute over the Dutch airline's ownership stake.

"Removing the ownership dispute from the relationship will only enhance our partnership," Killian said. He added that the agreement was reached after three-and-a-half years of negotiations between Northwest and KLM.

The two airlines were the first to establish an alliance, a practice that has become widespread between U.S.-based and foreign carriers. The alliance allows them to coordinate flights and to funnel passengers, for example, from Northwest's domestic routes into KLM's European service.
Killian said the operating alliance has added about $50 million to Northwest's annual operating income, an amount that could increase to $65 million this year.
"The alliance has been successful," Goldman Sachs analyst Glenn Engel said. "Hopefully this (agreement) will deepen the relationship."
"Theirs was basically the first alliance and so far-reaching, they had no choice but to patch up their differences," BT Securities analyst Vivian Lee added.
Killian said the two carriers may in the future integrate their large cargo operations. "There is a lot of potential to work together," he added.
Under the agreement, Northwest will buy KLM's stock in four tranches. The total cost of the KLM stock will be $1.07 billion to $1.17 billion.

The purchase price for the initial transaction will be determined by the volume-weighted average market price of Northwest shares for August 4, 5, 6, and 7. The maximum price will be $40 a share and the minimum $36.50.
The purchase price for the second, third and fourth portions will rise by about seven percent a year, Northwest said.

Northwest said the first transaction will include 6.8 million Northwest common shares and the remainder of the preferred shares still held by KLM. The second tranche will be 4.9 million shares of Northwest common stock; the third, 3.22 million shares of Northwest common stock, and the fourth, 10.05 million Northwest shares.
The two companies said they intend to finalize definitive agreements within 60 days. The final agreements are subject to approval by the boards of both companies.
